title: The Compass of Port Mahon
premise: In 1899, on the island of Port Mahon, Coral Sterling — a pearl diver's son indentured to the Aldous Trading Company since childhood — has survived fifteen years by knowing when to speak and when to stay silent. When the seasonal bridge closes and a drowned diver surfaces with company documents sewn into his coat, Coral becomes the only living witness who can connect the firm's ledgers to a decade of 'accidental' deaths in the pearl beds. Trapped on the island with the company's agents, its complicit magistrate, and the divers who once called him traitor for climbing into their masters' house, Coral must smuggle testimony, ledgers, and the dead man's widow off the island before the bridge reopens under the victors' control. He succeeds at terrible cost — burning his own indenture papers, losing the one person who believed him — and ends the century testifying in a colonial courtroom where his words are recorded but justice arrives only partially, leaving belonging as something he must build rather than be granted.
about_author: Paloma Iversen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company ledgers across Southeast Asian repositories. She writes from a converted pilot-house on the Baltic coast, where she keeps a jar of imperfect seed pearls on her desk as a reminder that value and damage are often the same thing.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Opening in the pearl beds of Port Mahon, 1899: Coral, now twenty-three and the company's trusted clerk-diver, records a dive log he knows is falsified. The emotional beat is quiet dread — he has learned which silences keep people safe, and this silence costs a diver his bonus. Establishes the island, the tides, and the ledger as instruments of power.

chapters.title: Indenture
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, moving through memory. A fever dream folds back to age eight, when his father's drowning debt made Coral property of Aldous Trading. We learn the arithmetic of belonging: fifteen years of service against a debt that never shrinks. Emotional beat: grief hardened into competence, and the first hint that the ledgers hide more than money.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The monsoon season closes the causeway bridge — the island's only link to the mainland — for five months. Mr. Quillan, the company factor, announces early closure 'for security,' stranding everyone. Coral notices the magistrate's men loading crates marked as ballast. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the island becomes a sealed room.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A diver named Eka Surya is pulled from the shallows, officially a diving accident. Coral, sent to inventory the body, finds documents stitched into the coat lining: pages from company ledgers listing deaths, payouts, and insurance claims on insured divers. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into purpose — the silences have names now.

chapters.title: The Widow's House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Sari, Eka's widow, a net-mender who reads the water better than any clerk. Coral brings her the truth instead of condolences. She reveals Eka had been copying ledgers for months, planning to carry them across the bridge. Emotional beat: two kinds of survivor recognizing each other; an alliance forms out of shared loss.

chapters.title: Quillan's Kindness
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Quillan promotes Coral, offering eventual freedom papers if he certifies Eka's death as misadventure. The offer is genuinely tempting — freedom, status, escape. Coral signs nothing and says less. Emotional beat: the corruption of power shown as generosity; Coral feels how easily he could become what owns him.

chapters.title: The Divers' Grudge
chapters.summary: Sari's POV. Sari approaches the divers' brotherhood to testify, and is refused: they remember Coral as the child who took the company's bread while their fathers drowned. Old wounds surface — Coral's father was blamed for a bed collapse that killed six men. Emotional beat: bitterness; the truth needs witnesses who hate the messenger.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, night work. Coral deciphers the full pattern: divers insured by the company die at rates no sea explains, each death triggering payouts Quillan routes through shell accounts in Port Mahon and beyond. His own father's name appears — not as debtor, but as a claimant defrauded. Emotional beat: rage arriving late, aimed at a system rather than a man.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Summoned to dine with Magistrate Orense, Coral performs gratitude while realizing the magistrate knows about the copied pages — it's a test dressed as courtesy. Orense offers a warning wrapped in philosophy: history belongs to whoever pays the historians. Emotional beat: terror managed through etiquette; Coral understands the clock is running.

chapters.title: Sari's Net
chapters.summary: Sari's POV. Sari organizes the women of the shore — menders, salters, widows — into a quiet courier web, moving pages inside repaired nets bound for fishing boats. She forces the divers' brotherhood to choose by shaming them with their own drowned dead. Emotional beat: power found in the work women were never thanked for.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the oldest ledger volume, Coral finds his father's marginal notes — the elder Sterling had been keeping his own count before he died. The discovery reframes everything: Coral inherited not just a debt but an unfinished testimony. Emotional beat: inheritance reversed; grief becomes mandate.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. One of the couriers is caught; a young salter breaks under questioning and gives up part of the network. Quillan, publicly merciful, privately lets Coral know he knows — and lets him go, a leash made of mercy. Emotional beat: guilt and paranoia; trust becomes a currency Coral can no longer verify.

chapters.title: Storm Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sari's POV. With boats confined to harbor, the plan shifts: the evidence must survive until the bridge opens, hidden in plain sight among the season's legitimate cargo. Sari proposes hiding the master copy inside the company's own export bales. Emotional beat: audacity born of desperation — smuggling truth through the thief's own warehouse.

chapters.title: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral dives the old wreck where his father died, recovering a sealed tin his father hid there — more pages, plus a letter naming the scheme's architect: not Quillan, but the company's mainland director, who built the insurance trade from Port Mahon upward. Emotional beat: the bottom of the mystery reached; the enemy grows larger than the island.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The informer, desperate to buy his family's safety, leads Orense's men to Sari. She burns her half of the archive rather than surrender it and is arrested for theft of company property. Coral watches from the counting room, forced to applaud the arrest. Emotional beat: the cost of silence paid in someone else's blood; self-loathing at its peak.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Key
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral trades the last thing he has — his certified silence, his perfect record — bribing a jailer with blackmail material to reach Sari's cell. He tells her about his father's tin. She tells him the divers are finally ready to speak, but only if Coral stands with them, not above them. Emotional beat: humility as strategy; leadership means standing inside the circle.

chapters.title: Brotherhood
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. On the beach at night, Coral returns his company seal to the divers and speaks his father's true count aloud. The brotherhood answers with their own dead's names. For the first time, testimony exists in living memory faster than Quillan can burn paper. Emotional beat: belonging achieved — not granted, built — at the moment of greatest danger.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The causeway reopens; the director himself arrives to inspect the island and close the century's books. Quillan moves to ship the incriminating volumes to the mainland for 'archival destruction.' Coral must get the father's tin and sworn depositions onto the director's own steamer — or lose everything to the victors' historians. Emotional beat: breathless momentum; the trap inverts.

chapters.title: Century's End
chapters.summary: Climax, Coral's POV. During the New Year's Eve crossing, Coral confronts the director aboard the steamer, swapping the doomed volumes for his father's tin via the cargo manifest, while Sari's network holds the shore witnesses ready. Quillan, offered a choice between his master and the record, hesitates — and his hesitation damns them both. The director is served with depositions as the year turns. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; the truth lands, bleeding.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, weeks later. A colonial commission hears testimony in the customs house. Justice is partial: the director flees to jurisdictions that won't extradite, Quillan takes the fall alone, and the compensation awarded to the widows is insultingly small. But the record stands — published, indexed, undeniable. Emotional beat: bitter victory; the point was never the verdict, it was the record.

chapters.title: Free Papers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The commission voids Coral's indenture as fraudulently extended. Holding freedom papers he no longer needs to escape, Coral chooses to stay — buying a share of the reorganized pearl beds with the divers' brotherhood. Emotional beat: quiet joy; freedom redefined as the right to remain and belong.

chapters.title: The Compass of Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, coda. Years later, Coral teaches the island's children to read both water and ledger, and places his father's restored count beside the official record in the new island archive — two truths, side by side. Sari mends nets beside the schoolhouse door. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept; the compass points home because he built the home it points to.
